location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 2: 'Then, without any all_reuse gate: today's --merge-only for Layers 2 and 5 ...')
issue: Interim Fase 2 drops today's step that refreshes stale Layer 2/5 per-version files ('Segarkan tiap (lapis, versi) yang masih rerun'). The only E2E-like re-check it keeps is for e2e cells. It also removes the all_reuse gate on the Layer 2/5 --merge-only. Neither merge_only() in ps-run-layer.py nor ps-aggregate.py checks freshness: merge_only copies whatever per-version files exist, and the aggregate trusts the canonical JSON. Version-first convergence makes this case normal. A patch made in 9.1's Fase 1 loop stales 1.7.8's and 8.1's Layer 2/5 files, which already converged, and no rule reopens those loops: the contract's Phase 2 entry check and per-version `clean` are deferred. The stale files are then merged into canonical flashlight/scenario files and credited.
implementation_impact: An implementer who follows the interim recipe writes run-phases.md so that Fase 2 merges stale Layer 2/5 evidence. `ready` can then be true while Layer 2 never ran against the patched source. This breaks the honesty law the spec's own Boundaries restate, and the gap is introduced by this slice: the all_reuse gate it removes was the only freshness guard on that merge.
suggestion: In Fase 2, before the merges, run one `--per-version` plan call over the in-scope versions. Run every non-adversarial, non-e2e layer still in `per_version[V].rerun` (Layers 1/2/5 via the normal per-version commands), or send those versions back to Fase 1, and only merge once no in-scope version lists flashlight/scenario/static as rerun. Add a doc rule that a patch in any loop reopens every version whose Layer 1/2/5 files it staled (the interim equivalent of the contract's Phase 2 entry check).

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration ('V's E2E loop ended ... while the plan's source_fingerprint equals the one printed by V's last E2E run this session')
issue: The interim ends V's E2E loop after a single run whenever the source has not changed, whatever the run produced. Interactive infra fixes that do not touch the module therefore can never be retried in the session: confirming an image pull and rerunning with --allow-image-pull (SKILL.md Lapis 2/4 flow), running `playwright install firefox` after a `browser-unavailable` record, freeing a stalled Docker daemon after a `crash`/`errors` record, or retrying a flaky BO login (`inconclusive-steps`). The contract is looser: it ends the loop only on `skipped`, a `blocked-*` step (`blocked-infra` needs two infra results in one session), `psm_e2e_enabled` false, or `--require` without e2e.
implementation_impact: The docs will tell the interactive orchestrator not to rerun E2E after Budi fixes the environment. The documented pull-confirmation flow is silently disabled for Layer 4, and the only way to retry is a dummy source edit or a new session. Both waste time, and the dummy edit also stales every other layer.
suggestion: Limit the fingerprint-equality rule to runs whose records for V are all conclusive (pass/fail) or headless. For interactive runs with inconclusive records, allow one retry after an explicit environment fix (the interim stand-in for the contract's two-strike blocked-infra), and state explicitly that the --allow-image-pull rerun is allowed.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 2: 'an appended fail re-enters Fase 1 for that version (interactive)')
issue: The loop-back is one clause, and the spec does not say where control returns after the re-entered Fase 1 loop ends. Open questions: is Fase 2 restarted from the top? Are the Layer 3 lenses respawned? They were spawned at Fase 2 start and may still be reviewing pre-patch source. Do the other versions' E2E cells, staled by the patch, run again? Do their Layer 2/5 files run again? The aggregate trusts `<module>-adversarial.json` with no freshness check. The contract's docs list explicitly requires 'Layer 3 spawned again after a loop-back' (adversarial-lens.md), and this spec omits it.
implementation_impact: run-phases.md will either continue to the merge/aggregate step after the patch, which credits an adversarial review of the old source and stale Layer 2/5/E2E evidence of other versions, or loop in an undefined way. In both cases the docs and the contract disagree.
suggestion: Add one sentence: after a Fase 2 loop-back, once the re-entered Fase 1 loop ends, restart Fase 2 from the top (re-plan, respawn Layer 3 unless the canonical plan reuses it, refresh stale Layers 2/5, rerun scoped e2e entries of versions whose E2E loop has not ended), and include the adversarial-lens.md 'respawn after loop-back' line in the docs task.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 1: 'V's loop ends when its rerun holds only adversarial/e2e ...')
issue: The end condition looks only at freshness. Right after V's stale Layers 1/2/5 run, their per-version files are fresh, so `rerun` holds only adversarial/e2e and the stated condition is met even when those files contain blocking findings. 'Patch and repeat as today' is not part of the termination rule. The contract's `clean` also requires that no Layer 1/2/5 per-version file holds a blocking finding, and today's docs loop 'sampai bersih'. The same applies to E2E: a fail with an unchanged fingerprint marks the loop ended, so V exits Fase 1 failing unless someone patches.
implementation_impact: An orchestrator that follows the literal rule moves to the next version, or to Fase 2, with known blocking Layer 2 or E2E failures unpatched. It spends the expensive Fase 2 boots on a module already known to fail, and the converge-per-version behavior the docs promise is lost.
suggestion: Make the interim end condition: `rerun` holds only adversarial/e2e, AND V's fresh Layer 1/2/5 per-version files hold no blocking finding (judged from the files, or from ps-aggregate's layer functions as the contract's `clean` does), AND V has no scoped e2e entry with reason `fail` unless the operator declines to patch (record that decision in the report).

location: Tasks > ps-e2e-run.py; Design Notes > Record / Child output in history mode ('a missing per-cell field is stored null')
issue: Today the child emits the version's tag as `tag` (not `image_tag`) and `scenario_notes` only at top level (not under `versions[V]`). The spec reads both as version-level child fields, yet its explicit ps-e2e-run task list (and the Boundaries bullet) enumerates many producer changes and omits these two. The shape check does not reject missing fields: it stores them as null. A null `image_tag` never equals the resolved tag, so every record is stale (`stale-tag`/`stale-source`). A null `scenario_notes` on a pass/fail record triggers `incomplete-record`. No task or AC tests a real child payload through to a passing gate-grade record. AC3 counts records only, and the plan/aggregate tests use hand-written records.
implementation_impact: An implementer who follows the enumerated task can ship a runner whose records never become passing gate-grade. All tests pass and nothing errors, and every cell reads stale or inconclusive forever. This is hard to diagnose because ps-run-layer quietly stores nulls.
suggestion: Add `image_tag` (renamed from `tag`, or emitted alongside) and per-version `scenario_notes` to the ps-e2e-run task explicitly. Add a test: a stub child emits a clean two-engine payload; ps-run-layer appends records; the plan reports no e2e rerun_matrix entry for those cells; the aggregate gives them `gate_grade: true` with reason null.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 1 iteration: run the stale layers, then 'if V has scoped e2e entries ... run ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e')
issue: The interim runs V's E2E cells in the same iteration as its stale Layers 1/2/5, whatever their outcome, including when Layer 2 has just shown the install failing. The contract (Plan > Phase 1) runs the E2E step only once V is clean. The spec neither adopts that gate nor names its absence as a deliberate slice deferral.
implementation_impact: Every dirty iteration spends a full PS+DB boot per version on E2E records that can only come out `install`-inconclusive or will be staled by the next patch. Combined with the fingerprint-based loop-ended rule, the E2E result recorded for the dirty state also suppresses a retry until a patch lands. This works against the slice's stated time-saving purpose.
suggestion: Run the E2E step only once V's Layers 1/2/5 are fresh and free of blocking findings in that iteration (interim `clean`), or state explicitly that this gate is deferred to CAP-1 and accept the cost.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (E2E loop-ended state held 'for the rest of the session' by the orchestrator)
issue: Deciding whether V's E2E loop has ended requires the LLM orchestrator to remember, per version and across a run that can last a day, the `source_fingerprint` printed by V's last E2E run and whether any run printed `skipped`. No script persists or derives this. Yet every record already carries `session` and `source_fingerprint`, and this slice makes `--session` mandatory on the plan without using it.
implementation_impact: After context compaction or a long session, the orchestrator may forget the last fingerprint. It then either reruns cells that should not run (cost) or skips cells that should (unproven cells it believes are already handled). Neither failure shows up in any script output.
suggestion: Derive it mechanically: V's E2E loop has ended when some configured cell of V has a history record whose `session` equals the current token and whose `source_fingerprint` equals the current one. Either the plan emits this per version (e.g. `per_version[V].e2e_ran_this_session`), which gives the required `--session` a use, or the docs tell the orchestrator to read it from the plan. Only the `skipped` flag would remain orchestrator memory.

location: I/O & Edge-Case Matrix rows 'Chromium-only' and 'Newer fail' (aggregate ready=false); Tasks > tests ('add the I/O matrix rows')
issue: These rows assert aggregate `ready=false` without fixing `--require` or the other layer inputs. The aggregate's default `--require` is every layer, so a fixture without flashlight/adversarial/scenario files gives `ready=false` regardless of E2E evidence. AC2 was tightened to `--require static,e2e` plus a conclusive static file, but the matrix rows the tests task says to add were not.
implementation_impact: Tests written from these rows pass even when per-cell gating is broken, for example when a Chromium-only history or a pass-then-fail history would wrongly count as passing. They therefore do not guard the CAP-2 behavior they exist for.
suggestion: Make every aggregate-side matrix row use the AC1 baseline (config 3x2, a conclusive static file for the three versions, `--require static,e2e`), and add the positive control: the same fixture with all six cells passing gives `ready=true`.
